title: The True Reason for the NFT Craze
description:
Everyone has a theory about NFTs: it was greed, it was a bubble, it was crypto bros chasing the next quick flip. Those explanations aren't wrong, but they miss the actual engine underneath the mania. This talk argues that NFTs succeeded not because of what they were — jpegs on a blockchain — but because of a much older human need they accidentally satisfied: the desire for legible status within a group.

Drawing on examples from PFP collections, gaming items, and ticketing, this talk unpacks the real mechanics behind the craze: verifiable scarcity as a social signal, community access as the actual product, and speculation as a form of collective storytelling. It's less about "digital ownership" and more about identity, belonging, and the oldest currency there is — being seen by the right people.
